newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Swiss Bank Corp. restructures domestic operation.
newsitem.headline: Swiss Bank Corp. restructures domestic operation.

text.p: Swiss Bank Corp. Wednesday announced sweeping changes to its domestic operations, including the shedding of some 1,700 jobs, that would lead to an expected loss of 1.9 billion Swiss francs ($1.5 billion) for 1996.
The bank expects the moves to improve the health of its ailing domestic operations, especially business with corporate clients, and boost overall profitability.

SBC said it would take extraordinary charges of about 3.3 billion francs ($2.7 billion) this year, but that would be offset by an expected profit of 1.4 billion ($1.1 billion) in 1996, compared with 1995's net profit of 1.05 billion francs ($847 million).

SBC, Switzerland's third-largest banking group, expects the restructuring of its domestic division -- including the closure or integration of 80 of 325 branches -- to lead to a boost to earnings of around 400 million francs ($323 million) in the next three years.
Most of the 1,700 jobs that will be eliminated over the next three years will be absorbed by natural attrition, retirements, internal transfers and retraining and flexible working hours.
Only 100 of the job losses will be due to the closing of branches, most of which employ only two to six people.
In addition to reorganizing its domestic operations, SBC will change the way it calculates possible losses on customer loans and revalue its own real estate portfolio.
